experiment: Plastic Optical Fiber Attenuation - Question Bank
description: Comprehensive 50-Question Physics Question Bank for Plastic Optical Fiber Attenuation

questions.question: What does optical fiber attenuation measure?
options: The reduction or loss of optical signal power as light travels through the fiber
The increase in wavelength of the light beam
The change in core diameter of the optical cable
The velocity increase of photons inside the waveguide
questions.answer: The reduction or loss of optical signal power as light travels through the fiber
questions.correct_option: The reduction or loss of optical signal power as light travels through the fiber
questions.explanation: Attenuation is the physical attenuation (decay) of optical power along an optical fiber due to absorption, scattering, and radiative losses.

questions.question: Which mathematical formula defines the total optical power attenuation (A_dB) in decibels?
questions.answer: A_dB = 10 · log10(P_in / P_out)
questions.correct_option: A_dB = 10 · log10(P_in / P_out)
questions.explanation: Decibel power attenuation is defined as A_dB = 10 · log10(P_in / P_out), expressing the ratio of input power to output power on a logarithmic scale.

questions.question: How is the attenuation coefficient (α) per unit length calculated from total attenuation A_dB and fiber length L?
questions.answer: α = A_dB / L
questions.correct_option: α = A_dB / L
questions.explanation: The attenuation coefficient α represents the loss normalized per unit distance: α = A_dB / L (expressed in dB/km or dB/m).

questions.question: When fiber length is measured in metres (L_m), how is the attenuation coefficient α in dB/km expressed?
questions.explanation: Because L_km = L_m / 1000, α_dB/km = A_dB / L_km = (1000 / L_m) · 10 · log10(P_in / P_out).

questions.question: What is the core material of standard Plastic Optical Fiber (POF)?
questions.answer: Polymethyl methacrylate (PMMA)
questions.correct_option: Polymethyl methacrylate (PMMA)
questions.explanation: Standard step-index POF utilizes polymethyl methacrylate (PMMA, acrylic) as its flexible, high-transparency core.

questions.question: What is the primary transmission window commonly used for PMMA-based Plastic Optical Fiber?
questions.answer: Visible red light (~650 nm)
questions.correct_option: Visible red light (~650 nm)
questions.explanation: PMMA polymer fibers exhibit an optical transmission window in the visible spectrum around 650 nm (red), where absorption minima occur.

questions.question: Under the Bouguer-Lambert-Beer law, how does optical power P_out decay with fiber length L for distributed loss α?
questions.explanation: Optical power undergoes exponential attenuation with propagation distance: P_out = P_in · 10^(-αL/10), matching the linear rate equation dP/dz = -α_p P.

questions.question: Why must input power (P_in) and output power (P_out) be measured in the same units before computing attenuation?
options: Because decibel loss is derived from a dimensionless power ratio
Because conversion to decibels is only possible for milliwatts
Because optical detectors only support one electrical unit at a time
Because powers must add up to 100%
questions.answer: Because decibel loss is derived from a dimensionless power ratio
questions.correct_option: Because decibel loss is derived from a dimensionless power ratio
questions.explanation: The argument of the logarithm (P_in / P_out) must be a dimensionless ratio; mixing mW and μW would introduce a 1000-fold error (+30 dB).

questions.question: What is Rayleigh scattering in plastic optical fibers caused by?
options: Microscopic density and refractive index fluctuations in the polymer matrix
Bending of the outer cable jacket
Total reflection at the metallic bench rail
Thermal expansion of the copper connectors
questions.answer: Microscopic density and refractive index fluctuations in the polymer matrix
questions.correct_option: Microscopic density and refractive index fluctuations in the polymer matrix
questions.explanation: Rayleigh scattering results from microscopic, sub-wavelength density fluctuations frozen into the amorphous polymer during manufacturing.

questions.question: How does Rayleigh scattering loss depend on the optical wavelength (λ)?
options: It is linearly proportional to λ
questions.answer: It is proportional to 1 / λ⁴
questions.correct_option: It is proportional to 1 / λ⁴
questions.explanation: Rayleigh scattering cross-section varies inversely with the fourth power of wavelength (1/λ⁴), resulting in much stronger scattering at shorter wavelengths.

questions.question: What causes the strong infrared absorption bands in PMMA plastic optical fiber?
options: Vibrational overtones and harmonics of carbon-hydrogen (C-H) molecular bonds
Electronic band transitions in silicon crystals
Conductance band electron scattering in copper
Magnetic dipole moments in the cladding
questions.answer: Vibrational overtones and harmonics of carbon-hydrogen (C-H) molecular bonds
questions.correct_option: Vibrational overtones and harmonics of carbon-hydrogen (C-H) molecular bonds
questions.explanation: C-H stretching vibration fundamentals and high-order overtones in PMMA create strong intrinsic absorption bands in the infrared region (>700 nm).

questions.question: What is macrobending loss in an optical fiber?
options: Radiative loss caused by curving the fiber below its permissible bend radius
Loss due to cable length being too long
Attenuation caused by thermal ambient changes
questions.answer: Radiative loss caused by curving the fiber below its permissible bend radius
questions.correct_option: Radiative loss caused by curving the fiber below its permissible bend radius
questions.explanation: Macrobending occurs when the fiber is curved with a macroscopic radius such that the angle of incidence at the outer core-cladding boundary falls below the critical angle, radiating light into the cladding.

questions.question: What is microbending loss in an optical fiber?
options: Loss caused by microscopic localized lateral deformations and axial stress along the core-cladding boundary
Reflection off the power meter LCD screen
Dispersion caused by multiple optical modes
Signal loss from slow photodetector response
questions.answer: Loss caused by microscopic localized lateral deformations and axial stress along the core-cladding boundary
questions.correct_option: Loss caused by microscopic localized lateral deformations and axial stress along the core-cladding boundary
questions.explanation: Microbending arises from microscopic repetitive mechanical imperfections, surface roughness, or lateral pinching that couple guided modes into radiating cladding modes.

questions.question: What typical attenuation coefficient (α) is expected for standard PMMA step-index POF at 650 nm?
questions.answer: Approximately 150 to 200 dB/km (0.15 to 0.20 dB/m)
questions.correct_option: Approximately 150 to 200 dB/km (0.15 to 0.20 dB/m)
questions.explanation: Standard PMMA step-index POF has an attenuation of ~150-200 dB/km at 650 nm, which is around 0.15-0.20 dB per metre.

questions.question: If input power P_in = 3.00 mW and output power P_out = 1.50 mW, what is the total attenuation in decibels?
questions.explanation: A_dB = 10 · log10(3.00 / 1.50) = 10 · log10(2) ≈ 10 · 0.30103 = 3.01 dB (halving of power corresponds to 3 dB loss).

questions.question: If input power P_in = 3.00 mW and output power P_out = 0.30 mW, what is the total attenuation in decibels?
If a 10.0 m optical fiber has a total attenuation of 1.80 dB, what is its attenuation coefficient in dB/km?
questions.answer: 180 dB/km
questions.correct_option: 180 dB/km

questions.question: What is the purpose of measuring reference power (P_in) before measuring the fiber output?
options: To establish a baseline coupled source power against which transmission loss is evaluated
To calibrate the physical guide rail ruler scale
To check whether the room ambient lighting is off
To determine the focal length of the detector lens
questions.answer: To establish a baseline coupled source power against which transmission loss is evaluated
questions.correct_option: To establish a baseline coupled source power against which transmission loss is evaluated
questions.explanation: Measuring P_in directly from the source or calibrated reference patch provides the known input power necessary to compute the decibel attenuation ratio.

questions.question: What happens to the Optical Power Meter reading when the optical source is switched OFF?
options: It reads zero (or subtle instrument dark noise floor)
It retains its previous measurement indefinitely
questions.answer: It reads zero (or subtle instrument dark noise floor)
questions.correct_option: It reads zero (or subtle instrument dark noise floor)
questions.explanation: With the light source de-energized, no optical photons strike the photodetector, yielding 0.00 mW (aside from negligible dark current).

questions.question: What happens to the power meter reading when the optical fiber is disconnected on the bench?
options: No light reaches the detector, producing zero measured output power
The meter reading increases due to free space propagation
The meter switches automatically into laser mode
questions.answer: No light reaches the detector, producing zero measured output power
questions.correct_option: No light reaches the detector, producing zero measured output power
questions.explanation: Disconnecting the fiber breaks the waveguide path, preventing source photons from arriving at the detector.

questions.question: Why should an optical transmitter be allowed to stabilize (warm up) prior to taking readings?
options: To ensure stable optical power output and eliminate semiconductor thermal drift
To allow the plastic optical fiber to melt slightly for better coupling
To discharge static electricity on the optical bench rails
To let the room reach ambient equilibrium
questions.answer: To ensure stable optical power output and eliminate semiconductor thermal drift
questions.correct_option: To ensure stable optical power output and eliminate semiconductor thermal drift
questions.explanation: Semiconductor LED/laser junctions undergo thermal shift during initial turn-on; warm-up ensures steady forward current and constant optical emission.

questions.question: What type of curve is observed when plotting measured output power P_out against fiber length L on linear axes?
questions.answer: An exponentially decaying downward curve
questions.correct_option: An exponentially decaying downward curve
questions.explanation: Because P_out = P_in · 10^(-αL/10), plotting power vs length on linear axes produces an exponential decay curve.

questions.question: What type of relationship is observed when plotting total decibel attenuation (A_dB) against fiber length L?
options: A linear relationship whose slope is the attenuation coefficient (α)
An exponential curve bending upward rapidly
A parabolic parabola with vertex at zero
An inverse hyperbola asymptotically approaching zero
questions.answer: A linear relationship whose slope is the attenuation coefficient (α)
questions.correct_option: A linear relationship whose slope is the attenuation coefficient (α)
questions.explanation: Since A_dB = α · L, total decibel loss is directly proportional to length, producing a straight line whose slope d(A)/dL = α.

questions.question: What is Fresnel reflection loss at the cleaved fiber end-facet?
options: Reflective loss caused by refractive index discontinuity between air (n≈1.0) and the polymer core (n≈1.49)
Scattering from impurities inside the optical detector silicon
Absorption by water vapour in the laboratory room
Loss caused by mechanical vibration of the optical bench
questions.answer: Reflective loss caused by refractive index discontinuity between air (n≈1.0) and the polymer core (n≈1.49)
questions.correct_option: Reflective loss caused by refractive index discontinuity between air (n≈1.0) and the polymer core (n≈1.49)
questions.explanation: At normal incidence, reflection R = [(n1 - n0) / (n1 + n0)]² ≈ [(1.49 - 1) / (1.49 + 1)]² ≈ 3.9% (~0.17 dB loss per facet) due to index mismatch.

questions.question: Why does lateral or angular misalignment of the input coupler degrade transmission?
options: It reduces coupling efficiency, as fewer incident rays fall within the fiber acceptance cone
It permanently alters the refractive index of the cladding
It shifts the laser emission wavelength to infrared
It increases electrical resistance of the power meter leads
questions.answer: It reduces coupling efficiency, as fewer incident rays fall within the fiber acceptance cone
questions.correct_option: It reduces coupling efficiency, as fewer incident rays fall within the fiber acceptance cone
questions.explanation: Misalignment causes rays to strike outside the fiber core area or at angles exceeding the acceptance cone (θ > θ_a), failing total internal reflection.

questions.question: How does dirt, dust, or fingerprints on the optical fiber facet affect the measurement?
options: They cause localized optical scattering and severe insertion loss
They decrease optical attenuation across the link
They transform multimode fiber into singlemode fiber
They have zero effect because polymer is immune to contamination
questions.answer: They cause localized optical scattering and severe insertion loss
questions.correct_option: They cause localized optical scattering and severe insertion loss
questions.explanation: Contaminants on the core face scatter and absorb light, introducing artificial extrinsic loss and corrupting baseline measurements.

questions.question: What is the typical core diameter of standard step-index plastic optical fiber compared to silica singlemode fiber?
options: POF core is very large (~980 μm to 1000 μm), whereas singlemode silica is ~9 μm
POF core is tiny (~1 μm), whereas silica is ~1 mm
POF has no core, only cladding
questions.answer: POF core is very large (~980 μm to 1000 μm), whereas singlemode silica is ~9 μm
questions.correct_option: POF core is very large (~980 μm to 1000 μm), whereas singlemode silica is ~9 μm
questions.explanation: Standard step-index POF has an enormous 1 mm outer diameter with a ~980 μm core, making alignment easy with visible light.

questions.question: What is a key advantage of POF's large core diameter in laboratory experiments?
options: High coupling tolerance and easy mechanical alignment without sub-micron positioning equipment
Ability to transmit terahertz radio waves
Immunity to all forms of macrobending
questions.answer: High coupling tolerance and easy mechanical alignment without sub-micron positioning equipment
questions.correct_option: High coupling tolerance and easy mechanical alignment without sub-micron positioning equipment
questions.explanation: With a ~1 mm core, light can be coupled efficiently with inexpensive connectors and relaxed alignment tolerances.

questions.question: If a student records P_in = 2.50 mW and P_out = 2.50 mW for an ideal 0 m link, what is total attenuation?
questions.explanation: A_dB = 10 · log10(2.50 / 2.50) = 10 · log10(1) = 0.00 dB (zero attenuation corresponds to unity power transmission).

questions.question: If 10% of input power is lost during propagation (so P_out = 0.90 · P_in), what is the total attenuation?
If 90% of input power is lost during propagation (so P_out = 0.10 · P_in), what is the total attenuation?
If 99% of input power is lost during propagation (P_out = 0.01 · P_in), what is the total attenuation?
What is the primary trade-off of Plastic Optical Fiber compared to Silica Glass Optical Fiber?
options: POF has much higher attenuation (~180 dB/km vs ~0.2 dB/km) but offers superior flexibility, ruggedness, and low installation cost
POF is much more brittle and shatters upon touch
POF cannot guide visible light wavelengths
POF requires cryogenic cooling to operate
questions.answer: POF has much higher attenuation (~180 dB/km vs ~0.2 dB/km) but offers superior flexibility, ruggedness, and low installation cost
questions.correct_option: POF has much higher attenuation (~180 dB/km vs ~0.2 dB/km) but offers superior flexibility, ruggedness, and low installation cost
questions.explanation: While silica fiber has ultra-low loss (~0.2 dB/km at 1550 nm) for long-haul networks, POF's higher loss restricts it to short-distance links (<100 m) where mechanical toughness is key.

questions.question: How does the cutback method determine fiber attenuation in professional laboratory practice?
options: By measuring output power, cutting the fiber back to a short reference length, and taking the ratio of measured powers without disturbing input coupling
By slicing the fiber horizontally to observe core cross-section under an electron microscope
By increasing laser voltage until the fiber burns back
By measuring reflection while cutting off the power supply
questions.answer: By measuring output power, cutting the fiber back to a short reference length, and taking the ratio of measured powers without disturbing input coupling
questions.correct_option: By measuring output power, cutting the fiber back to a short reference length, and taking the ratio of measured powers without disturbing input coupling
questions.explanation: The cutback method measures long-length power P2, then cuts back to short reference length L1 (measuring P1) without changing input launch conditions, yielding α = [10/(L2-L1)] log10(P1/P2).

questions.question: Why is the cutback technique effective at eliminating connector and coupling loss errors?
options: Because input coupling conditions remain strictly unchanged between long and short measurements
Because it cools the fiber down to absolute zero
Because cutting the fiber eliminates all internal Rayleigh scattering
Because it converts multimode light into singlemode light
questions.answer: Because input coupling conditions remain strictly unchanged between long and short measurements
questions.correct_option: Because input coupling conditions remain strictly unchanged between long and short measurements
questions.explanation: Since the input launch coupling chuck is untouched, input coupling efficiency η_in is identical in both measurements and cancels out in the power ratio.

questions.question: What physical unit is used to express optical power in the digital meter?
questions.answer: Milliwatts (mW) or Microwatts (μW)
questions.correct_option: Milliwatts (mW) or Microwatts (μW)
questions.explanation: Optical power is the time rate of radiant optical energy transfer, measured in milliwatts (mW) or microwatts (μW), or in logarithmic dBm.

questions.question: How is optical power in milliwatts (mW) related to microwatts (μW)?
questions.answer: 1 mW = 1000 μW
questions.correct_option: 1 mW = 1000 μW
questions.explanation: Milli means 10⁻³ and micro means 10⁻⁶; thus, 1 mW = 1000 μW.

questions.question: If a power meter reads 450 μW, what is the equivalent power in mW?
How is optical power expressed in dBm related to power in milliwatts (P_mW)?
questions.answer: P_dBm = 10 · log10(P_mW / 1 mW)
questions.correct_option: P_dBm = 10 · log10(P_mW / 1 mW)
questions.explanation: dBm is decibels referenced to 1 milliwatt: P_dBm = 10 · log10(P_mW / 1 mW). For example, 1 mW = 0 dBm.

questions.question: What is 0 dBm in milliwatts?
questions.answer: 1.0 mW
questions.correct_option: 1.0 mW
questions.explanation: By definition, 0 dBm corresponds to 1.0 mW (10 · log10(1.0) = 0 dBm).

questions.question: If an input power is +3 dBm and output power is 0 dBm, what is the link attenuation in dB?
questions.answer: 3 dB
questions.correct_option: 3 dB
questions.explanation: Attenuation in dB is the difference between input and output levels in dBm: A = P_in(dBm) - P_out(dBm) = 3 dBm - 0 dBm = 3 dB.

questions.question: Why does bending a plastic fiber into a tight loop (small radius of curvature) increase attenuation?
options: Guided rays strike the core-cladding boundary at angles steeper than the critical angle and escape as radiation loss
The copper core experiences work hardening and increased resistance
The wavelength of light shifts into the ultraviolet regime
The speed of light inside the core drops to zero
questions.answer: Guided rays strike the core-cladding boundary at angles steeper than the critical angle and escape as radiation loss
questions.correct_option: Guided rays strike the core-cladding boundary at angles steeper than the critical angle and escape as radiation loss
questions.explanation: Tight curvature alters the local boundary orientation so rays exceed the critical angle (θ < θ_c), refracting into the cladding as radiative macrobending loss.

questions.question: What role does the cladding layer play in reducing attenuation in optical fibers?
options: It provides a lower refractive index boundary (n2 < n1) enabling total internal reflection while protecting the core from surface contamination
It amplifies light through stimulated emission
It filters out red wavelengths to only pass infrared
It acts as an electrical ground plane
questions.answer: It provides a lower refractive index boundary (n2 < n1) enabling total internal reflection while protecting the core from surface contamination
questions.correct_option: It provides a lower refractive index boundary (n2 < n1) enabling total internal reflection while protecting the core from surface contamination
questions.explanation: The lower-index cladding (n2 < n1) establishes the boundary for total internal reflection and isolates the evanescent optical field from dirt and moisture.

questions.question: In a laboratory experiment, if a student forgets to switch ON the optical transmitter, what will the power meter indicate?
options: 0.00 mW (No optical signal reaching the sensor)
questions.answer: 0.00 mW (No optical signal reaching the sensor)
questions.correct_option: 0.00 mW (No optical signal reaching the sensor)
questions.explanation: Without light emission from the transmitter, the photodetector generates zero photocurrent, reading 0.00 mW.

questions.question: If measured output powers are 2.88 mW (at 1 m) and 2.44 mW (at 5 m) for P_in = 3.00 mW, what trend is verified?
options: Transmitted optical power decreases monotonically as fiber length increases
Transmitted power is completely independent of length
The fiber generates optical power from ambient heat
questions.answer: Transmitted optical power decreases monotonically as fiber length increases
questions.correct_option: Transmitted optical power decreases monotonically as fiber length increases
questions.explanation: As propagation length increases, cumulative absorption and scattering losses increase, causing monotonic decrease in transmitted power.

questions.question: What is the numerical aperture (NA) of standard step-index POF typically around?
options: High NA (~0.45 to 0.50), providing a wide acceptance angle (θ_a ≈ 27° to 30°)
questions.answer: High NA (~0.45 to 0.50), providing a wide acceptance angle (θ_a ≈ 27° to 30°)
questions.correct_option: High NA (~0.45 to 0.50), providing a wide acceptance angle (θ_a ≈ 27° to 30°)
questions.explanation: Standard PMMA POF features a high index contrast (n1 ≈ 1.492, n2 ≈ 1.402), yielding a large NA ≈ 0.50 and wide acceptance cone.

questions.question: How does the large numerical aperture of POF affect coupling efficiency from an LED source?
options: It significantly improves coupling efficiency because the wide acceptance cone captures a large fraction of diverging LED rays
It prevents any LED rays from entering the core
It converts the LED into a monochromatic laser
questions.answer: It significantly improves coupling efficiency because the wide acceptance cone captures a large fraction of diverging LED rays
questions.correct_option: It significantly improves coupling efficiency because the wide acceptance cone captures a large fraction of diverging LED rays
questions.explanation: A high NA (0.50) creates an acceptance cone of ~60° full angle, capturing substantial radiant flux from divergent surface-emitting LEDs.

questions.question: What is an important precaution when handling plastic optical fibers in an undergraduate physics lab?
options: Avoid sharp kinks or bending below minimum bend radius, and keep connector end facets clean
Never expose the outer jacket to visible room lighting
Always submerge the cable in water before powering the laser
Connect the fiber only when power supply is set to 220 V AC
questions.answer: Avoid sharp kinks or bending below minimum bend radius, and keep connector end facets clean
questions.correct_option: Avoid sharp kinks or bending below minimum bend radius, and keep connector end facets clean
questions.explanation: Sharp bends induce permanent mechanical crazing and radiation loss, while dirty facets degrade coupling efficiency.

questions.question: If linear regression of A_dB against L (in metres) yields a slope m = 0.180 dB/m, what is the attenuation coefficient in dB/km?
questions.answer: 180 dB/km
questions.correct_option: 180 dB/km
questions.explanation: Since 1 km = 1000 m, α_dB/km = slope_dB/m · 1000 = 0.180 · 1000 = 180 dB/km.

questions.question: In optical engineering, why is decibels (dB) preferred over percentage transmission for cascaded links?
options: Because decibel losses of successive components add linearly instead of multiplying
Because decibels eliminate all physical loss
Because decibels work only with integer numbers
questions.answer: Because decibel losses of successive components add linearly instead of multiplying
questions.correct_option: Because decibel losses of successive components add linearly instead of multiplying
questions.explanation: In decibels, total loss A_total = A_fiber + A_coupler + A_splice (addition of dB terms instead of multiplying fractional transmission factors).
